claim: The 30.22 release is the first whose MySQL tokenizer ends a `#` / `--` line comment only at a newline, and installing any version in the pinned range gives that behavior.
source_excerpt: The `30.22` floor is the first release whose MySQL tokenizer ends a `#` / `--` line comment only at a newline. Older MySQL tokenizers end it at a carriage return as well, so `SELECT n FROM widgets # x` + carriage return + `'` + newline raised `TokenError` while the guard — which first turns that carriage return into a space in `_mysql_parse_sql` — accepted it: `first_sql_keyword` and the guard would see the same statement differently. From 30.22 the three dialects' tokenizers also treat nested block comments as their engines do (Postgres nests; MySQL and SQLite end a comment at the first `*/`).
verify_against: sqlglot's MySQL tokenizer behavior at 30.21 and 30.22 and the installed version's handling of `SELECT n FROM widgets # x\r'\n`
verify_hint: Tokenize `"SELECT n FROM widgets # x\r'\n"` with sqlglot's MySQL tokenizer on the installed version and check the nested-block-comment cases `/* a /* b */ c */` under postgres, mysql and sqlite

source_excerpt: A table reference with no schema or catalog qualifier whose own name (after `normalize_identifiers` for the dialect) is a CTE visible in its scope under sqlglot's scope analysis (`traverse_scope`) does not count as a catalog table, whatever its name: on Postgres, `WITH pg_recent AS (…) SELECT * FROM pg_recent` is a data query.

claim: `is_introspection_query` returns `True` before any parse when `first_sql_keyword` is `SHOW`, returns `False` for a `SHOW`-led statement the tokenizer rejects, excludes no CTE reference on any exception from identifier normalization or scope analysis (logging its type at INFO), and propagates any other parser exception.
source_excerpt: **Fail-open to `False`.** Unlike the guard (which fails *closed* to `UnsafeSqlError`), this classifier returns `False` on a sqlglot `ParseError` / `TokenError` or a `None` parse result (logged at `INFO`), except that a statement whose `first_sql_keyword` is `SHOW` returns `True` before any parse. A `SHOW`-led statement the tokenizer rejects has no leading keyword, so it returns `False` (the guard fails closed on the same input and the database rejects it, so it never returns rows). An exception from identifier normalization or scope analysis excludes no CTE reference — every table counts toward the catalog check — and its type is logged at `INFO`.
verify_hint: Check every `except` clause and log call in `is_introspection_query` in `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py`
